subject.title: feat(mxc): add Windows MXC sandbox backend

question: After the registration-mode bug is fixed, should OpenClaw accept the exact `@microsoft/mxc-sdk@0.7.0`/`node-pty` dependency graph and MXC SDK argv-carried config boundary for this official external Windows sandbox plugin?
rationale: The code guard is mechanically fixable, but accepting native executor dependencies and process-argv config exposure is a security and release ownership decision automation cannot make.

options.title: Fix Guard, Then Approve Exact Head
options.body: Require the full-registration guard and regression test first, then approve the dependency graph and argv boundary for the exact reviewed head if secops accepts the risk.

options.title: Pause For Non-Argv Transport
options.body: Hold the PR until upstream MXC or OpenClaw provides a config transport that does not expose the encoded sandbox envelope through process argv.

options.title: Defer First-Party MXC Packaging
options.body: Keep MXC outside the official plugin release path until the native dependency and sandbox boundary are mature enough for first-party support.

recommendation.title: Fix Guard, Then Approve Exact Head
recommendation.body: Require the full-registration guard and regression test first, then approve the dependency graph and argv boundary for the exact reviewed head if secops accepts the risk.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR is assigned to steipete and the remaining non-mechanical question is release/security acceptance.
